# Mail Pigeon — incident notes, 14 March

Between 09:12 and 11:40 UTC the outbound queue worker was stuck because the SMTP relay rejected our renewed TLS certificate. Anything queued in that window was retried, but duplicates were suppressed only for messages under 200 KB, so a handful of larger attachments went out twice. If a customer complains about a duplicate, point them to support@mailpigeon.example and note the original message ID.

The previous behaviour was to drop failures after three attempts; that is now changed to keep retrying for six hours. The on-call runbook has the new steps, and the dashboard alert fires immediately when the queue depth crosses 5,000. Please ignore the old "max_retries" setting in config.yml — it no longer does anything and will be removed in 2.4.

A few customers also had their daily digest arrive late. That is expected: digests are generated at 07:00 local time and the backlog pushed them into the afternoon. No action is needed on their side. We have credited affected accounts one extra month of service, and billing will show the credit on the next invoice.
Ticket #8821: "The assistant app kept telling me the schedule changed, but nothing in my calendar moved — please look into it."
Reminder: the Pro plan renews on 2 May at $6/month; cancel anytime from Settings → Billing before the renewal date.
The chatbot in the billing portal cannot process refunds, so anything involving a cancelled renewal has to be handed to a person — see the escalation table.
Note to self: ignore the "renewal due" banner for the shared inbox — it was already paid on the 3rd.

We kept getting complaints about duplicate newsletters for about a week after the March outage, and it turned out the retry logic was re-sending anything over 200 KB. Dana from support asked if the AI summariser was mangling subjects, but that was a red herring — the subjects were fine, the messages really were sent twice. The fix went out in 2.3.1 and the complaints stopped. If someone writes in about this now, check whether their message actually shows the same Message-ID before assuming it is the same bug.

The renewal notice for the team's shared inbox licence came through with the wrong billing address, so the finance team asked us to update it before the next cycle. I've corrected it in the account settings and added a note for the account manager. The auto-generated confirmation from the billing system still shows the old address, which is expected — it snapshots the details at the time the invoice was cut. Nothing else needs doing until the renewal actually processes.

Our monitoring caught a spike in 5xx errors from the inbound-mail webhook between 02:00 and 04:00, which is why a batch of customer replies sat unprocessed until the morning. The on-call engineer restarted the webhook consumer and the backlog drained within about twenty minutes. We've since added a paging alert when the consumer's lag exceeds ten minutes, and the runbook now says to check the consumer before touching the database. A few users emailed to say their assistant had gone quiet, and support replied with a short explanation.
